question.text: Rolle's theorem is applicable in the interval [-2,2] for the function

solution.text:
If we take $f(x)=4 x^{4}$, then
(i) $f(x)$ is continuous in (-2,2)
(ii) $f(x)$ is differentiable in (-2,2)
(iii) $f(-2)=f(2)$ So, $f(x)=4 x^{4}$ satisfies all the conditions of Rolle's theorem therefore $\exists$ a point $c$ such that
$f^{\prime}(c)=0$
$\Rightarrow \quad 16 c^{3}=0 \Rightarrow c=0 \in(-2,2)$
